'''Li Fanghua''' ({{lang-zh|s=李方华}}; 6 January 1932 – 24 January 2020) was a Hong Kong-born Chinese physicist.<ref name="lion">{{cite news|url=http://www.china.org.cn/english/culture/60664.htm |title=Li Hailed as Top Woman Scientist  |newspaper=China Daily |date=  April 2, 2003}}</ref> She was a member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], [[The World Academy of Sciences]], and the [[International Union of Crystallography]].<ref name="lion" /> She was also the director of [[Chinese Society of Physics]] and China Union of Crystallography, and an editor of the ''[[Journal of Chinese Electron Microscopy Society]]'', ''[[J. Electron Microscopy]]'', ''[[Chinese Physics Letter]]'', and ''[[Chinese Journal of Physics]]''.

Li won the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science]] in 2003.<ref name="lion" /><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cas.cn/hy/xshd/200303/t20030322_1690722.shtml |script-title=zh:贺李方华院士获"联合国教科文组织世界杰出女科学家成就奖"报告会举行|newspaper=Chinese Society of Physics |date= 2003-03-22|language=zh }}</ref> She was fluent in English, French, German, Japanese, and Russian.<ref name="tiger">{{cite news|url= http://news.sina.com.cn/c/cul/2007-07-18/083212225413s.shtml|script-title=zh:李方华：显微科学的"半边天" |newspaper=Sina |date=2007-07-18 |language= zh}}</ref>

==Biography==
=== Studies and research ===
The [[Cultural Revolution]] (1966–1976) interrupted her studies; ultimately she accessed the Leningrad University's library to continue studies.<ref name="lion" />

== Honors and awards ==

* 2001 Elected one of the Top 10 Outstanding Women by the Chinese Academy of Sciences<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-03 |title=Li Fanghua |url=https://www.asiaresearchnews.com/content/li-fanghua |access-date=2026-06-25 |website=Asia Research News |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Li was married to fellow physicist [[Fan Haifu]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.beijingreview.com.cn/2009news/guonei/keji/2010-03/17/content_255250.htm |script-title=zh:李方华：科学对性别无偏见 |newspaper=Beijing Review |date= 2010-03-17 |language= zh}}</ref>
